newsitem.title: India: CRICKET-SYMCOX AND DE VILLIERS RESCUE SOUTH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SYMCOX AND DE VILLIERS RESCUE SOUTH AFRICA.

text.p: Tailenders Pat Symcox and Fanie de Villiers rescued South Africa with a half-century stand after they collapsed against India's spin trio in the first test on Thursday.

Coming together with South Africa reeling at 119 for seven in reply to India's first innings of 223, Symcox and de Villiers put on 63 for the eighth wicket to lead their side to 202 for eight at the close on the second day.
Fine bowling by left-arm spinner Sunil Joshi and leg-spinners Anil Kumble and Narendra Hirwani, allied to two dubious umpiring decisions, raised Indian hopes of a useful first innings lead.
But Symcox (32) and de Villiers (40 not out) staged a fightback that left the match evenly poised after two days.
Joshi has taken four for 42, Kumble two for 68 and Hirwani two for 38.
India, resuming at the overnight 215 for eight, were bowled out for 223 within half an hour of the start of play.
Donald, who finished with four for 37, and fellow paceman de Villiers, who had two for 55, each took one more wicket.
The worst fears about the pitch at the Sardar Patel Stadium proved true when the Indian spinners came on after just 10 overs by the medium pacers.
The ball turned, especially from Joshi, though it was Kumble who sent back both openers, Andrew Hudson and the consistent left-hander Gary Kirsten.
In only his third over, Kumble had Kirsten stretched forward to drive. He missed and Nayan Mongia brought off a smart leg-side stumping.
Hudson misread a googly and was trapped lbw plumb in front.
Then came two controversial lbw dismissals.

Umpire S.K. Bansal gave out captain Hansie Cronje and Darryl Cullinan lbw, both stretching well forward to balls pitched outside the leg stump and neither offering a stroke. Hirwani claimed Cronje and Cullinan fell to Joshi.
South African were deep in trouble at 119 for seven, still 104 runs behind India's first innings total, when de Villiers joined Symcox for the best partnership of the match so far.
Symcox, who had played with restraint, finally fell to a rash stroke and Donald filled his place to see the session through to end of play.
